summary: This defines a WeatherEntry class, a small immutable data holder that bundles one day's date, temperature in Celsius, and sky condition into a single object. A weather app can then store many of these in a list and run stream pipelines over them.

lines.text: The date is stored as text in ISO order (year-month-day), which sorts correctly as a plain string. Marking the field final means it can never change after the object is built.

lines.code: private final double celsius;   // temperature in °C
lines.text: Temperature uses double because readings carry fractional degrees, such as 21.5.

lines.code: private final String condition; // e.g., Sunny, Rainy, Cloudy
lines.text: The condition is a simple label that later stream filters can compare against, such as keeping only the rainy days.

lines.text: The constructor is the only way to supply values, so every WeatherEntry is fully populated the moment it exists.
The keyword this distinguishes the field named date from the constructor parameter of the same name.
Because the fields are private, getter methods give read-only access to the data from outside the class. Stream code calls these through method references like WeatherEntry::getDate.
This getter is what a mapToDouble pipeline uses to pull out temperatures for converting to Fahrenheit or averaging.
This annotation tells the compiler you intend to replace a method inherited from Object, so a typo in the method name becomes a compile error instead of a silent bug.
Overriding toString gives the object a readable form, so printing an entry or a whole list shows the actual weather data rather than a memory address.
The escape sequence '\'' is a single-quote character, which wraps the date in quotes to make the printed output easier to read.
